title: Bellarmine: Catholics, against all the heretics, hold free choice in moral good as dogma
source_text: LI. Istud videre est apud Bellarminum. Controversia est, inquit, inter Catholicos omnes ab una parte, & Hereticos omnes hujus temporis (neque enim hac in re vel apud nostros, vel apud adversarios ulla est opinionum varietas) sitne homo in statu naturae lapsae liberi arbitrii in bono morali eligendo, & malo evitando, sive quod idem est in praeceptis morum observandis, aut praevaricandis. Et quidem Catholici omnes, tum veteres tum recentiores, tanquam dogma fidei Catholicae praedicant partem affirmantem. De libero Arbitrio lib. 5. cap. 13.
pass_a_gloss: LI. That is seen in Bellarmine. The controversy is, he says, between all Catholics on one part, and all the Heretics of this time (for neither in this matter either among ours, or among the adversaries is there any variety of opinions) whether man in the state of fallen nature be of free choice in choosing moral good, and avoiding evil, or which is the same in observing, or transgressing the precepts of morals. And indeed all Catholics, both old and more recent, preach as a dogma of the Catholic faith the affirmative part. On free Choice book 5. chapter 13.
pass_b_english: This is seen in Bellarmine. 'The controversy,' he says, 'is between all Catholics on one side and all the heretics of this time on the other (for on this point there is no variety of opinion either among our own or among our adversaries): whether man in the state of fallen nature has free choice in choosing moral good and avoiding evil, or, what is the same, in keeping or breaking the precepts of morals.
And all Catholics, both the old and the more recent, proclaim the affirmative as a dogma of the Catholic faith.' On free choice, book 5, chapter 13.
